name: Hospital
visual_anchor: Massive multi-story hospital complex at dusk with illuminated red emergency bay signage, flashing ambulance beacons reflecting across wet asphalt, and bright sterile windows towering into the night sky.
core_traits: Provides continuous round-the-clock intensive medical treatment, surgery, and emergency care
Filled with distinctive smells of antiseptic solutions, sound of heart rate monitors, and rolling gurney wheels
Organized into specialized clinical departments such as triage, radiology, cardiology, and operating suites
Features a dedicated emergency vehicle entrance and rooftop helipad for critical medical airlifts

facts_and_myths.claim: Hospitals intentionally use calming colors like soft green and pale blue on surgical scrubs and walls.
facts_and_myths.explanation: These hues reduce eye strain for surgeons operating under intense lamps and counteract visual fatigue caused by staring at red blood.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Before the mid-20th century, most hospital operating attire was pure white.

facts_and_myths.claim: Modern hospital emergency rooms operate strictly on a first-come, first-served basis.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Emergency departments utilize a standardized triage system where medical urgency and life threat dictate care priority over arrival time.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The triage concept originated on battlefields to rapidly categorize wounded soldiers.

name: Police Station
visual_anchor: Urban brick police precinct front entrance flanked by blue spherical lamps, patrol cruisers with strobing red and blue lightbars parked out front, and radio transmission towers rising above the rooftop.
core_traits: Acts as the operational base for municipal law enforcement officers, detectives, and dispatchers
Features a secure booking reception, holding cells, interview rooms, and an evidence locker
Constantly echoes with the crackle of dispatch radios, ringing emergency lines, and jingling duty belt keys
Maintains armed patrol vehicles parked in secured perimeter lots ready for rapid deployment

facts_and_myths.claim: A person under police interrogation has an absolute right to remain silent under standard constitutional procedures.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Known widely as Miranda rights or cautions, individuals in custody must be informed of their legal right against self-incrimination before formal questioning.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Holding cells in precincts are temporary and rarely hold detainees for more than a few days before court appearances.

facts_and_myths.claim: Police stations must wait 24 to 48 hours before accepting a missing person report.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Law enforcement agencies accept missing person reports immediately without mandatory waiting periods, especially when minors or vulnerable individuals are involved.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Early intervention within the first 48 hours is statistically critical in finding missing persons safely.

name: Fire Station
visual_anchor: Red-brick firehouse with giant arched bay doors flung open, revealing gleaming scarlet fire engines with polished chrome bumpers and coiled yellow hoses under overhead spotlighting.
core_traits: Houses specialized firefighting apparatus, ladder trucks, water tankers, and paramedic gear
Equipped with dormitory living quarters, a communal kitchen, training yard, and equipment drying racks
Maintains instantaneous response readiness triggered by high-volume klaxon alarm tones
Historically famous for brass sliding poles allowing firefighters to drop swiftly from living quarters to truck bays

facts_and_myths.claim: Traditional firehouses kept Dalmatian dogs because they naturally bonded with and guarded carriage horses.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Dalmatians ran alongside horse-drawn fire carriages to keep stray animals away and guarded the horses from theft while firefighters battled blazes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Dalmatians are still celebrated as the universal mascot of fire stations worldwide.

facts_and_myths.claim: All modern fire stations continue to install and mandate the use of traditional brass sliding poles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many modern stations have replaced brass poles with slides or single-story floor plans to reduce ankle, knee, and spine injuries caused by pole descents.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The first fire pole was invented in Chicago in 1878 by Captain David Kenyon.

name: Post Office
visual_anchor: Classic stone municipal post office with bronze postal boxes, customer service service counters behind protective glass, sorting trays piled with parcels, and delivery vans lined up at the loading dock.
core_traits: Processes, sorts, and dispatches domestic and international mail, postcards, and freight parcels
Features rows of private lockboxes, digital scale counters, and postage stamp dispensing kiosks
Characterized by the rustle of paper envelopes, automated barcode scanner beeps, and rubber stamp thuds
Dispatches uniformed postal carriers and motorized delivery fleets on daily localized routes

facts_and_myths.claim: The universal post horn symbol on European postal buildings dates back to horns blown by mounted mail riders.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Postilions blew curved brass horns to announce arrival into towns and warn oncoming traffic to yield right-of-way to the mail coach.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The post horn remains an iconic logo for postal systems across Germany, Sweden, and Austria.

facts_and_myths.claim: Post offices are permitted to open and read private sealed first-class letters at random without warrants.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Strict postal privacy laws and international treaties forbid postal staff from opening sealed correspondence without specific judicial search warrants.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Only packages exhibiting hazardous leaks, explosives, or custom declarations undergo routine non-warranted inspection.

name: City Hall
visual_anchor: Imposing neoclassical civic building featuring grand stone columns, a high clock tower rising into twilight, public steps adorned with bronze lanterns, and municipal flags fluttering above the pediment.
core_traits: Serves as the administrative seat of local municipal government and the office of the mayor
Houses the city council debating chamber, clerk records department, and urban planning bureaus
Issues civil marriage licenses, business permits, building registrations, and voter credentials
Frequently faces a prominent public plaza used for civic ceremonies and democratic demonstrations

facts_and_myths.claim: Medieval city halls in Europe frequently featured towering belfries to ring out municipal alarms and curfew signals.
facts_and_myths.explanation: City belfry bells signified civic independence from feudal lords and regulated daily work shifts and city gate closures.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many historic Flemish and Belgian belfries are designated UNESCO World Heritage sites.

facts_and_myths.claim: City halls only hold administrative meetings and are entirely closed to the general public during working hours.
facts_and_myths.explanation: City halls are public institutions where residents regularly attend open council sessions, pay municipal taxes, and obtain public records.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Thousands of couples choose historic city halls each year as venues for civil wedding ceremonies.

name: Courthouse
visual_anchor: Solemn courtroom interior framed by dark oak paneling, elevated judicial bench, ornate bronze scales of justice sculpture, and sunlight streaming through tall clerestory windows over rows of spectator benches.
core_traits: Conducts formal civil lawsuits, criminal trials, bail hearings, and legal adjudications
Furnished with an elevated judge's bench, witness stand, jury box, and attorney tables
Governed by strict courtroom decorum, the strike of the wooden gavel, and swearing under oath
Connected via secure underground subterranean tunnels or passages to holding facilities

facts_and_myths.claim: The blindfolded Lady Justice statue holding a balance scale and sword symbolizes impartiality in the application of law.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The blindfold signifies that justice should be rendered objectively without prejudice regarding wealth, power, or social status.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The figure is derived from the ancient Roman goddess Justitia.

facts_and_myths.claim: Judges in every country around the world routinely bang a wooden gavel to call the courtroom to order.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The gavel is primarily used in the United States; judges in the United Kingdom, Canada, and most European civil law courts do not use gavels at all.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: British judges maintain order solely by verbal admonitions and judicial authority.

name: Prison
visual_anchor: High concrete security walls topped with coils of razor wire, illuminated by sweeping high-intensity halogen watchtower searchlights into a misty night sky with barred cell windows in the distance.
core_traits: Enforces involuntary confinement and rehabilitation for individuals convicted of legal crimes
Secured with reinforced steel bars, electronic interlocks, barbed wire perimeters, and observation towers
Operates on rigid daily schedules with headcounts, recreation yard hours, and cafeteria meal calls
Monitored by armed correctional officers, surveillance camera matrices, and metal detection gates

facts_and_myths.claim: The Panopticon design was created so a single guard in a central tower could observe all inmates without them knowing if they were watched.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Philosopher Jeremy Bentham designed the circular panopticon prison in the late 18th century to induce constant self-monitoring among prisoners.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Stateville Correctional Center in Illinois was one of the few facilities actually built on the panopticon model.

facts_and_myths.claim: The terms 'prison' and 'jail' refer to the exact same administrative type of penal institution.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Jails are local facilities holding detainees awaiting trial or serving short misdemeanors under one year, whereas prisons house convicted felons serving long-term sentences.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Jails are typically run by county sheriffs, while prisons are managed by state or federal departments.

name: Embassy
visual_anchor: Gated diplomatic compound flying a foreign national flag, protected by ornamental iron palisades, security checkpoint booths, bulletproof glazing, and manicured diplomatic reception lawns.
core_traits: Serves as the primary diplomatic headquarters of an ambassador representing their home nation in a host capital
Handles diplomatic negotiations, international treaties, citizen passport services, and travel visa approvals
Protected under international treaty law from unwarranted entry or search by host nation authorities
Staffed by foreign service attaches, political officers, consular agents, and sovereign marine guards

facts_and_myths.claim: Under the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, embassy premises are inviolable by host country police.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Local authorities cannot enter an embassy without explicit permission from the head of the diplomatic mission.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: This legal protection also applies to diplomatic correspondence and diplomatic mail pouches.

facts_and_myths.claim: An embassy compound legally becomes the physical sovereign territory of the sending country.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The land remains sovereign soil of the host nation, but enjoys special extraterritorial immunities and diplomatic protection by bilateral agreement.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: If an embassy is decommissioned, host country jurisdiction resumes immediately.

name: Military Base
visual_anchor: Expansive secured military installation at dawn, showing concrete guard entry gates with vehicle tire spikes, hangars housing tactical aircraft, parade grounds, and perimeter patrol towers.
core_traits: Houses military personnel, munitions arsenals, tactical equipment, and tactical command centers
Guarded by armed sentries, automated vehicle barricades, and secure perimeter fencing
Contains living barracks, supply depots, weapon firing ranges, and tactical maintenance hangars
Operates under strict military command hierarchy and specialized security classifications

facts_and_myths.claim: Many major military bases function as self-contained cities with their own schools, hospitals, grocery stores, and post offices.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Base exchanges, commissaries, and housing developments allow military families and service members to live entirely within the base perimeter.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Fort Liberty in North Carolina accommodates over 50,000 active-duty personnel.

facts_and_myths.claim: Military bases are open for regular commercial civilian flights to land whenever public airports are congested.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Military airfields operate under strictly controlled defense airspace and prohibit civilian aircraft without prior diplomatic or emergency clearance.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Unauthorized entry into military airspace triggers immediate armed interceptor scrambles.

name: Public Library
visual_anchor: Quiet cavernous library reading room with towering mahogany bookshelves stretching to vaulted ceilings, green banker lamps casting emerald pools of light over long polished tables.
core_traits: Lends books, multimedia, audiobooks, and historical periodicals to the general public free of charge
Enforces a traditional atmosphere of quiet study, intellectual research, and digital workstation access
Organized using classification systems such as the Dewey Decimal or Library of Congress catalogs
Staffed by professional librarians assisting patrons with reference inquiries and literacy programs

facts_and_myths.claim: Philanthropist Andrew Carnegie funded the construction of over 2,500 public libraries worldwide between 1883 and 1929.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Known as Carnegie Libraries, these institutions revolutionized open-shelf access so patrons could browse books directly.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 1,600 Carnegie library buildings were erected across the United States alone.

facts_and_myths.claim: Libraries are obsolete repositories that no longer provide services beyond paper books.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Modern public libraries offer digital e-book lending, 3D printing labs, internet access, community workshops, and archival databases.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Public library visits in many metropolitan areas continue to outpace cinema admissions.

name: Town Square
visual_anchor: Vibrant historic town square paved with ancient cobblestones, centered around an ornate bubbling stone fountain with outdoor cafe umbrellas, clock towers, and historic merchant facades.
core_traits: Acts as the open central gathering point and civic crossroads of an urban community
Bordered by major civic institutions such as city hall, cathedral, cafes, and markets
Hosts seasonal festivals, open-air farmers markets, public gatherings, and holiday celebrations
Filled with pedestrian activity, street performers, resting benches, and ornamental statues

facts_and_myths.claim: Ancient Greek city-states used open town squares called agoras as centers for athletic, musical, and political life.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Agora of Athens was the cradle of direct democratic discourse where citizens gathered to debate laws and conduct commerce.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Philosophers like Socrates spent their days conversing with citizens in the Agora.

facts_and_myths.claim: Town squares are always built in rigid square geometric shapes without exception.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many world-famous town squares are circular, trapezoidal, or irregular, adapting to historic topography and road convergences.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Piazza del Campo in Siena, Italy, is famously shaped like an open scallop shell.

name: Community Center
visual_anchor: Modern glass and timber community center with brightly lit multipurpose gymnasium, meeting rooms hosting workshops, craft displays in the lobby, and outdoor community garden plots.
core_traits: Provides accessible neighborhood facilities for youth clubs, senior activities, and civic workshops
Contains multipurpose indoor halls, art studios, recreational courts, and meeting rooms
Serves as a polling station during elections and an emergency evacuation shelter during crises
Offers community fitness classes, after-school tutoring, and cultural celebration gatherings

facts_and_myths.claim: Community centers are frequently designated as temporary disaster relief shelters during floods or hurricanes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Their spacious gymnasiums, emergency backup generators, and industrial kitchens make them ideal for housing displaced residents.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Red Cross coordinates shelter operations through municipal community centers.

facts_and_myths.claim: Community centers require expensive paid country club memberships for neighborhood residents to enter.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Community centers are publicly subsidized municipal amenities designed to be affordable or free to all local citizens regardless of income.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many programs for children and seniors are funded entirely by local tax revenues.

name: Parliament Building
visual_anchor: Majestic monumental legislative palace crowned with an illuminated central dome, sweeping marble facade reflected in a quiet ornamental basin, and legislative banners under twilight skies.
core_traits: Houses the elected national legislative body responsible for drafting, debating, and voting on laws
Features a central debating chamber arranged in opposing benches or semicircular hemicycles
Contains the ceremonial speaker's rostrum, parliamentary mace, and translation galleries
Serves as the focal point of national statecraft, political debates, and constitutional reform

facts_and_myths.claim: In the British Houses of Parliament, red lines on the carpet separate opposing parties by two sword-lengths.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tradition holds that Members of Parliament were forbidden from crossing the line to prevent physical duels during heated debates.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: This is widely believed to be the origin of the English idiom 'to toe the line'.

facts_and_myths.claim: Parliament buildings never permit ordinary citizens to watch legislative debates in person.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Democratic parliaments maintain public galleries where citizens, journalists, and tourists can observe floor proceedings live.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Debates are also broadcast live on public parliamentary television networks.

name: High School
visual_anchor: Sunlit suburban high school campus with brick wings, rows of student lockers lining wide linoleum hallways, a football field with bleachers, and yellow school buses queued at the curb.
core_traits: Delivers secondary education to adolescent students preparing for higher education or vocational careers
Features classroom wings, science laboratories, a school library, cafeteria, and gymnasium
Regulated by ringing period bells, hall passes, locker combinations, and athletic pep rallies
Hosts extracurricular activities including marching band, debate teams, drama plays, and varsity sports

facts_and_myths.claim: Secondary education became widely tuition-free and legally compulsory in most Western nations during the early 20th century.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The 'high school movement' in the early 1900s rapidly transformed secondary schooling from an elite luxury to a universal public right.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: High school graduation rates rose from under 10% in 1910 to over 80% by the late 20th century.

facts_and_myths.claim: High school diplomas around the world have universally identical standardized curricula and testing formats.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Curricula vary drastically by country, ranging from the British A-Levels and German Abitur to the French Baccalaureat and US AP exams.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The International Baccalaureate (IB) was created to establish a transferable global secondary diploma.

name: University Campus
visual_anchor: Sprawling university quadrangle framed by ivy-draped Gothic stone lecture halls, historic clock tower, students resting on manicured lawns, and pathways leading to high-tech science laboratories.
core_traits: Conducts undergraduate and postgraduate education, academic research, and degree conferrals
Comprises lecture halls, research institutes, student dormitories, dining halls, and academic faculties
Features prominent green quadrangles, bell towers, varsity athletic facilities, and vast research libraries
Fosters specialized academic scholarship across humanities, engineering, medicine, and social sciences

facts_and_myths.claim: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco, founded in 859 AD, is recognized by UNESCO as the world's oldest continually operating university.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It was established by Fatima al-Fihri as a mosque and madrasa before evolving into an internationally renowned center of higher learning.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The University of Bologna, founded in 1088, is considered the oldest university in Europe.

facts_and_myths.claim: The term 'campus' originated as an acronym for collegiate academic studies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: 'Campus' is the Latin word for 'field' or 'plain', first applied in the 18th century to describe the open grounds of Princeton University.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Prior to this usage, collegiate grounds in Europe were usually called 'colleges' or 'courts'.

name: Public Park
visual_anchor: Sprawling green urban park framed by distant skyscraper skylines, winding asphalt jogging paths lined with leafy oak trees, an ornamental duck pond, and scattered wooden park benches.
core_traits: Provides open natural green space within urban centers for public recreation, exercise, and leisure
Equipped with walking trails, children's playgrounds, picnic lawns, dog parks, and park benches
Maintains public landscape features such as flower beds, tranquil ponds, and historic bandstands
Offers respite from city noise, vehicle emissions, and dense concrete architecture

facts_and_myths.claim: Central Park in New York City was entirely landscaped artificially with hundreds of thousands of planted trees, artificial lakes, and sculpted earth.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Designers Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux reshaped swampy, rocky terrain into an idealized pastoral landscape starting in the 1850s.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: More gunpowder was used to blast rock in Central Park than during the Battle of Gettysburg.

facts_and_myths.claim: Urban public parks produce net negative economic value because park land cannot generate property taxes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Parks significantly boost surrounding real estate valuations, provide flood stormwater absorption, and lower healthcare costs through active public recreation.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Proximity to a well-maintained park typically increases adjacent residential property value by 10% to 20%.

name: Cemetery
visual_anchor: Tranquil historic cemetery cloaked in morning mist, rows of weathered marble and granite tombstones beneath weeping willows, ornate wrought-iron gates, and quiet gravel paths.
core_traits: Serves as consecrated municipal or religious ground for burying deceased persons and interring ashes
Marked by headstones, family crypts, mausoleums, columbarium walls, and memorial plaques
Maintains a quiet, contemplative atmosphere dedicated to commemoration and ancestral remembrance
Lined with perpetual green lawns, mature shade trees, and fresh memorial floral bouquets

facts_and_myths.claim: In Victorian times, cemeteries were designed as scenic landscaped rural parks where families regularly held leisurely weekend picnics.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Before public city parks became common, rural cemeteries like Pere Lachaise in Paris and Mount Auburn in Boston were popular recreational escapes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Guidebooks were published specifically to help Victorian tourists tour celebrity graves.

facts_and_myths.claim: The word 'graveyard' and 'cemetery' are strictly synonymous with identical historical etymologies.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Historically, a graveyard was directly attached to a churchyard, whereas a cemetery was an independent secular or municipal burial ground situated outside church grounds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word 'cemetery' derives from the Greek 'koimeterion', meaning 'sleeping place'.

name: Wastewater Treatment Plant
visual_anchor: Sprawling industrial water reclamation facility beside a river, showcasing massive circular settling clarifier basins, bubbling aeration tanks, and intricate networks of green pipes and pumping stations.
core_traits: Purifies municipal domestic sewage and industrial wastewater before returning clean effluent to waterways
Utilizes primary mechanical settling screens, secondary biological bacteria breakdown, and chemical disinfection
Identified by large open circular clarifier tanks with rotating scraper bridges and aerator bubbles
Protects downstream river ecosystems and public municipal drinking water sources from contamination

facts_and_myths.claim: Microscopic beneficial bacteria and microorganisms do the vast majority of organic waste consumption in modern sewage treatment.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In secondary aeration tanks, trillions of aerobic microbes digest dissolved human waste, converting it into harmless cell biomass and carbon dioxide.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: This biological sludge is subsequently converted into rich agricultural fertilizer or biogas fuel.

facts_and_myths.claim: Treated wastewater from modern plants is simply dumped raw without destroying harmful pathogens.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Final stages include intensive ultraviolet (UV) radiation or chlorination that obliterates bacteria and viruses before discharge.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Advanced tertiary plants produce water purer than standard municipal tap water.

name: Recycling Center
visual_anchor: Vast industrial sorting warehouse filled with rushing conveyor belts, robotic optical sorting arms separating plastics, massive compressed bales of crushed aluminum cans and corrugated cardboard.
core_traits: Sorts, processes, and packages recyclable municipal materials like metals, paper, cardboard, and plastics
Operates high-speed conveyor belts, eddy-current aluminum separators, magnetic pulleys, and balers
Filled with rumbling mechanical vibrations, clattering glass bottles, and hydraulic press hums
Diverts tons of reusable commodities from landfills and supplies raw feedstocks to manufacturing mills

facts_and_myths.claim: Recycling an aluminum beverage can saves roughly 95% of the electrical energy required to make a new can from raw bauxite ore.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Extracting and smelting primary aluminum is extraordinarily energy-intensive, whereas remelting recycled aluminum uses a small fraction of the power.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: An aluminum can can be recycled, remanufactured, and back on supermarket shelves within 60 days.

facts_and_myths.claim: Placing non-recyclable garbage or greasy pizza boxes in recycling bins is harmless because sorting machines easily clean them.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Wishcycling causes severe grease contamination in paper pulpers and clogs sorting conveyor machinery, forcing entire batches of recyclables to be landfilled.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Optical sorters use infrared spectroscopy to identify polymer types in milliseconds.

name: Power Plant
visual_anchor: Gigantic industrial electrical generating station at dusk with hyperbola-curved cooling towers billowing clean white steam plumes, high-voltage transformer substations humming beneath lattice pylon towers.
core_traits: Generates utility-scale electrical energy supplied to municipal and national power transmission grids
Utilizes diverse primary energy sources including hydro turbines, thermal steam, nuclear fission, or gas turbines
Dominated by massive steam turbines, spinning synchronous generators, and high-voltage step-up switchyards
Characterized by a persistent low-frequency electrical hum and billowing condensation clouds from cooling towers

facts_and_myths.claim: The white clouds emerging from the giant curved cooling towers of nuclear and coal power plants are pure water vapor.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cooling towers release evaporated cooling water used to condense steam back into liquid, containing zero radioactive materials or particulate soot.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The iconic hyperbolic cooling tower shape was engineered to maximize natural draft airflow.

facts_and_myths.claim: Electricity generated at a power plant flows directly into household wall sockets without voltage transformations.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Voltage is stepped up to hundreds of thousands of volts for transmission over long cables to minimize energy loss, then stepped down repeatedly before reaching homes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: High-voltage transmission lines typically operate between 110,000 and 765,000 volts.

name: Weather Station
visual_anchor: Isolated high-altitude meteorological outpost on a windswept hill, featuring spinning anemometer cups, doppler radar radome sphere, automated weather balloon launch gantry, and solar radiation sensors.
core_traits: Continuously records atmospheric temperature, barometric pressure, wind velocity, humidity, and rainfall
Equipped with white louvered Stevenson screens, ultrasonic anemometers, rain gauges, and satellite telemetry dishes
Launches hydrogen or helium-filled weather balloons carrying radiosondes twice daily into the stratosphere
Feeds critical real-time atmospheric data into global forecasting supercomputers and aviation warning systems

facts_and_myths.claim: Weather balloons launched from meteorological stations regularly ascend over 30 kilometers into the stratosphere before bursting.
facts_and_myths.explanation: As the balloon rises through thinner air, internal gas expands until the latex stretches to the size of a two-story house and ruptures, dropping instruments by parachute.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Over 800 weather stations launch radiosonde balloons simultaneously worldwide at 00:00 and 12:00 UTC.

facts_and_myths.claim: Modern computerized weather satellites have completely eliminated the need for ground-based weather stations.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Satellites cannot directly measure ground-level barometric pressure or surface microclimates, making surface station calibration absolutely essential.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Ground station historical records provide the core baseline for measuring century-scale climate trends.

name: Astronomical Observatory
visual_anchor: Silvery hemispherical observatory dome atop a remote mountain peak under a brilliant starry Milky Way galaxy, dome slit open revealing a giant optical reflecting telescope bathed in soft red interior night lights.
core_traits: Houses powerful optical or radio telescopes designed to study celestial bodies, stars, galaxies, and planets
Built on remote mountain summits or arid plateaus to escape urban light pollution and atmospheric turbulence
Features a motorized rotating hemispherical dome with an opening slit aligned with telescope tracking motors
Illuminated internally only with dim red light emitting diodes to preserve astronomers' night vision adaptation

facts_and_myths.claim: Modern major astronomical observatories use adaptive optics with lasers to counteract blurry atmospheric twinkling in real time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Artificial laser guide stars measure atmospheric turbulence thousands of times per second, dynamically flexing thin telescope mirrors to produce crystal-sharp imagery.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Adaptive ground telescopes can often match or exceed the resolution of space telescopes.

facts_and_myths.claim: Professional research astronomers spend all night peering directly through glass optical eyepieces with their eyes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Astronomers view computer monitors in remote control rooms receiving digital data from ultra-sensitive cryogenically cooled CCD sensors.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Most astronomers can operate modern mountain telescopes remotely from continents away.

name: Blood Donation Center
visual_anchor: Bright sterile clinical donor room with comfortable reclining vinyl donor chairs, gentle rhythmic whir of blood bag rocking scales, tube sealers, and volunteer refreshments table with juice and biscuits.
core_traits: Collects, tests, separates, and stores human whole blood, platelets, and plasma from volunteer donors
Furnished with reclining phlebotomy chairs, computerized apheresis machines, and refrigerated centrifuge banks
Maintains strict hygienic protocols, sterile single-use needle collection kits, and donor hemoglobin screenings
Supplies life-saving blood transfusions to emergency trauma wards, surgical suites, and cancer therapies

facts_and_myths.claim: A single pint of whole blood donated at a center can be separated into components to save up to three lives.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Blood is centrifuged into red blood cells, platelets, and liquid plasma, each serving distinct patient therapy needs.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Red blood cells have a refrigerated shelf life of roughly 42 days, while platelets must be used within 5 to 7 days.

facts_and_myths.claim: Donating whole blood depletes the donor's body of fluid and blood cells permanently.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The human body replaces lost fluid volume within 24 to 48 hours and regenerates all donated red blood cells within several weeks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Healthy donors can safely give whole blood every eight weeks in most jurisdictions.

name: Public Archive
visual_anchor: Climate-controlled subterranean repository with mobile rolling compact shelving units holding thousands of acid-free preservation boxes, scholars wearing white cotton gloves inspecting illuminated historical parchments.
core_traits: Preserves irreplaceable historical government documents, founding charters, treaties, and public records
Maintains strict temperature, relative humidity, and ultraviolet lighting controls to prevent paper degradation
Equipped with secure research reading rooms, digitization scanner suites, and document restoration labs
Requires researchers to handle original centuries-old manuscripts under supervision with archival gloves

facts_and_myths.claim: Major national archives store foundational parchment charters in argon or nitrogen gas cases to prevent oxygen decay.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Inert gas encasements stop oxidation, insect activity, and moisture damage to invaluable founding documents.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The original US Declaration of Independence is stored in a bulletproof, inert gas vault beneath the National Archives in Washington.

facts_and_myths.claim: Public archives are private government vaults that completely forbid ordinary citizens from inspecting records.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most democratic public archives are legally open to genealogists, academic historians, and citizens researching ancestry or government decisions.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Census records become publicly unsealed after standard statutory embargo periods (typically 72 years).

name: Municipal Water Tower
visual_anchor: Towering bulbous steel municipal water reservoir elevated high above a suburban landscape on crisscrossed steel trestle legs, painted with the town's name, glowing under a golden sunset.
core_traits: Stores potable treated municipal drinking water at elevation to pressurize the city's water distribution network
Relies entirely on gravity and hydrostatic pressure rather than continuous pumps to maintain tap water pressure
Features a massive spherical or toroidal steel tank perched atop high lattice pillars or central concrete shafts
Guarantees sufficient emergency water volume and hydrologic head during peak usage and municipal firefighting

facts_and_myths.claim: Water towers maintain water pressure in household taps even during widespread electrical grid blackouts.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because water is already elevated dozens of meters high, natural hydrostatic gravity head provides continuous pressure without electric pumps.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Every foot of water tower height generates approximately 0.433 pounds per square inch (psi) of water pressure.

facts_and_myths.claim: Water towers continually pump fresh water directly into each house's pipes in real time.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pumps fill the tower during nighttime low-demand periods, and the tower drains during daytime peak hours to balance municipal system demand.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many communities paint local mascots or town slogans on their water towers as civic landmarks.

name: Botanical Conservatory
visual_anchor: Majestic Victorian wrought-iron and curved glass greenhouse cathedral glowing warmly from within at dusk, surrounded by lush tropical palms and misty humid air visible through the panes.
core_traits: Houses rare, exotic, and climate-sensitive tropical flora under controlled indoor microclimates
Constructed from intricate wrought iron, steel rib arches, and thousands of clear glass panels
Maintains specialized automated misting systems, elevated heating pipes, and humid subtropical air
Features elevated canopy catwalks allowing visitors to observe towering palm crowns and orchids

facts_and_myths.claim: The Palm House at Kew Gardens in London, built in the 1840s, was the first large-scale structural use of wrought iron in a public building.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Engineered by Richard Turner and Decimus Burton, the design borrowed techniques from shipbuilding to support unprecedented glass spans.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It still houses some of the oldest potted plants in cultivation, including an ancient cycad potted in 1775.

facts_and_myths.claim: Conservatories rely exclusively on natural solar warmth and never use artificial heating during harsh winters.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Extensive subterranean boilers and water radiator networks are critical to keep delicate tropical plants from freezing when outside temperatures plummet.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Historic conservatories burned tons of coal daily in dedicated basement boiler rooms.

name: Supreme Court
visual_anchor: Stately classical marble courthouse facade carved with allegorical friezes of law, monumental central entrance flanked by solemn sculpted sentinels, bathed in dramatic dawn light.
core_traits: Acts as the apex judicial authority and ultimate court of legal appeal within a sovereign nation
Interprets constitutional disputes, judicial reviews of national legislation, and landmark civil rights cases
Features a formal curved or straight mahogany bench where a panel of justices preside in black robes
Does not retry witness testimony or hold jury trials, focusing strictly on questions of constitutional law

facts_and_myths.claim: Decisions rendered by a nation's supreme court set binding legal precedent for all lower regional courts.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Under the doctrine of stare decisis, lower courts are legally compelled to adhere to the rulings and interpretations established by the highest court.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Supreme Court justices in the US serve lifetime appointments unless they retire or face impeachment.

facts_and_myths.claim: Every legal appeal filed by any citizen must automatically be heard and decided by the Supreme Court.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Supreme courts receive thousands of petitions annually but exercise discretionary jurisdiction, selecting only a tiny fraction (often under 1%) involving pivotal constitutional questions.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The US Supreme Court grants hearing to only about 80 of the 7,000 cases appealed each year.

name: Presidential Palace
visual_anchor: Gilded neoclassical presidential mansion surrounded by wrought-iron perimeter gates, pristine gravel motorcade driveway, fluttering national standard, and illuminated formal reception chandeliers.
core_traits: Functions as the official working office and ceremonial residence of the national head of state or government
Contains executive offices, the cabinet war room, formal banquet state dining rooms, and diplomatic reception halls
Protected by round-the-clock ceremonial elite guard sentries, perimeter snipers, and high-tech security rings
Hosts visiting heads of foreign nations, ambassador credential ceremonies, and state treaty banquets

facts_and_myths.claim: The White House in Washington, DC, was set ablaze by British troops during the War of 1812 and had to be extensively reconstructed.
facts_and_myths.explanation: In August 1814, British forces burned the mansion; only the exterior stone walls survived, which were later whitewashed and rebuilt.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: First Lady Dolley Madison famously saved a full-length portrait of George Washington before fleeing the burning mansion.

facts_and_myths.claim: A presidential palace belongs as personal private real estate to whichever president is currently in office.
facts_and_myths.explanation: State executive mansions are sovereign public property belonging to the nation and maintained as historic heritage institutions by civil service agencies.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Incoming heads of state must relocate out of the executive residence immediately upon their successor's inauguration.

name: Coast Guard Station
visual_anchor: Coastal maritime rescue station perched on a rocky headland, featuring concrete slipways launching orange all-weather lifeboats, high-frequency radio masts, and twin search and rescue helicopters on tarmac pads.
core_traits: Conducts maritime search and rescue operations, coastal border enforcement, and maritime navigational aid safety
Equipped with specialized high-speed surf rescue boats, cutters, cutter moorings, and coastal patrol aircraft
Operates continuous 24/7 marine radio monitoring on international VHF distress frequencies like Channel 16
Maintains rapid all-weather deployment readiness to rescue shipwreck victims, stranded sailors, and capsized vessels

facts_and_myths.claim: Modern coast guard surf rescue boats are designed to be self-righting if completely rolled over by giant breaking waves.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Watertight superstructure geometry and a low center of gravity automatically roll the vessel back upright within 8 to 12 seconds if capsized.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The engines continue running even when momentarily upside down in heavy seas.

facts_and_myths.claim: Coast guard bases only operate during daylight hours and cease rescue missions during severe ocean storms.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Coast guard stations specialize in operating precisely when maritime weather is most dangerous, maintaining round-the-clock all-weather readiness.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The US Coast Guard's unofficial historic motto is 'You have to go out, but you don't have to come back.'

name: Animal Shelter
visual_anchor: Bright suburban municipal animal welfare center with clean glass-fronted adoption suites, volunteer dog-walking agility yards, cat climbing trees, and friendly reception desks displaying adoption profile cards.
core_traits: Rescues, houses, rehabilitates, and facilitates the adoption of lost, abandoned, or surrendered domestic animals
Features indoor-outdoor dog kennels, specialized feline communal rooms, and veterinary clinic examination bays
Filled with barking greetings, purring cats, stainless steel food bowls, and leash-walking volunteers
Administers vaccinations, microchipping, and spay/neuter surgeries prior to pet adoption

facts_and_myths.claim: Microchips implanted in shelter animals do not contain GPS tracking devices.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Shelter microchips use passive RFID technology that transmits an identification code only when scanned at close range by a handheld wand.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The ID number links to a registered database containing the owner's phone number and address.

facts_and_myths.claim: All animal shelters are gloomy pounds where pets are automatically euthanized within three days.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The global animal welfare movement has established widespread 'no-kill' shelters and extensive foster volunteer networks prioritizing lifelong placement.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Many shelters achieve live-release rates exceeding 90% through community foster networks.

name: Civil Defense Bunker
visual_anchor: Subterranean fortified blast bunker carved into solid granite bedrock, sealed by a massive circular steel blast door with locking lugs, yellow tactical floodlights illuminating air filtration conduits.
core_traits: Engineered to protect personnel and command leadership from nuclear blast overpressure, radiation, or bomb strikes
Constructed deep underground with thick reinforced concrete walls, blast doors, and shock-absorbing dampers
Self-contained with independent diesel generators, NBC (nuclear, biological, chemical) air scrubbers, and deep water wells
Stocked with long-shelf-life rations, emergency communication lines, and survival bunking bays

facts_and_myths.claim: Switzerland maintains enough civil defense fallout bunker spaces to shelter more than 100% of its entire national population.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Swiss federal law mandated fallout shelter construction in residential buildings starting in the Cold War, creating millions of fortified spaces.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Lucerne Sonnenberg Tunnel bunker was designed to accommodate up to 20,000 citizens in an emergency.

facts_and_myths.claim: A standard home basement provides total, complete protection against high-radiation nuclear blast waves without reinforcement.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Ordinary house walls provide minimal blast overpressure resistance and allow gamma radiation infiltration unless shielded by substantial earth, lead, or concrete.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: At least 3 feet of packed earth or 2 feet of concrete is required to reduce gamma radiation by 99%.

name: Central Bank
visual_anchor: Imposing fortress-like national central bank headquarters constructed from rusticated stone, heavy bronze portals, deep security grilles, and armored bullion delivery trucks escorted by tactical security.
core_traits: Controls national monetary policy, sets benchmark interest rates, and oversees currency money supply
Acts as the government's fiscal agent and the lender of last resort to commercial banking institutions
Safeguards national sovereign gold bullion reserves and foreign exchange foreign currency assets
Supervises national financial stability, commercial bank solvency, and banknote circulation printing

facts_and_myths.claim: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York holds the largest depository of monetary gold bullion on Earth in its bedrock vault.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Resting 80 feet below street level on Manhattan bedrock, it safeguards hundreds of billions of dollars in gold bars for foreign nations and central banks.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: No single individual knows all parts of the vault combinations, and gold is moved between compartments by weight.

facts_and_myths.claim: Central banks are ordinary retail banks where members of the general public can open personal checking accounts.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Central banks do not serve individual consumers; their clients are strictly commercial banks, foreign central banks, and sovereign governments.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The oldest central bank is Sweden's Riksbank, established in 1668.

name: Public Fountain Plaza
visual_anchor: Sunlit grand urban plaza centered around an immense cascading stone fountain with sculpted bronze sea nymphs, soaring water jets catching iridescent rainbows, surrounded by granite seating terraces.
core_traits: Features large ornamental water jets, tiered cascades, and sculpted basins serving as a civic focal point
Surrounded by pedestrian promenades, outdoor cafe tables, street musicians, and resting spectators
Provides natural evaporative microclimate cooling and peaceful white-noise masking of city traffic sounds
Frequently serves as a traditional gathering spot where passersby make wishes by tossing small coins

facts_and_myths.claim: Over a million euros in coins are tossed into Rome's Trevi Fountain each year, which are collected daily to fund charity food programs.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Roman Catholic charity Caritas receives all coins swept from the fountain to subsidize supermarket vouchers and shelters for the needy.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Legend holds that tossing a coin over your left shoulder with your right hand ensures you will return to Rome.

facts_and_myths.claim: Public civic fountains pump fresh drinking water straight from municipal water supply mains and dump it into the storm sewers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Modern civic fountains utilize closed-loop recirculating pump filtration systems that continuously clean and reuse the same water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Automated wind sensors lower water jet heights on gusty days to prevent spraying pedestrians.

name: International Airport
visual_anchor: Vast airport terminal concourse with sweeping glass curtain walls overlooking runways at twilight, wide-body jetliners docked at illuminated jet bridges, and runway approach lights stretching to the horizon.
core_traits: Accommodates domestic and cross-border commercial passenger aviation flights and cargo air freight
Includes vast terminal gate concourses, customs inspection checkpoints, passport control, and baggage claims
Dominated by the roaring roar of jet engines, runway taxiway signage, and airport flight display boards
Features dual-direction parallel runways, taxiway networks, and specialized aircraft ground service vehicles

facts_and_myths.claim: Runway numbers painted on airport tarmac correspond directly to magnetic compass headings rounded to the nearest ten degrees.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A runway numbered '09' points eastward toward 90 degrees magnetic, while '27' at the opposite end points westward toward 270 degrees.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Because Earth's magnetic north pole drifts over decades, airports periodically repaint their runway numbers.

facts_and_myths.claim: Airport security luggage scanners rely on powerful ultraviolet lamps to see through passenger suitcases.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Security screening units use dual-energy X-ray beams and computed tomography (CT) scanners that differentiate organic materials from dense metals by atomic density.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Organic explosives appear in distinct orange color coding on airport X-ray operator displays.

name: Train Station
visual_anchor: Monumental glass and steel train shed covering multiple passenger platforms, sleek aerodynamic high-speed trains idling beside classic passenger cars, illuminated departure flipboards clicking overhead.
core_traits: Serves as the arrival and departure terminus for commuter, intercity, and high-speed passenger rail lines
Features raised passenger boarding platforms, ticket barriers, waiting concourses, and luggage services
Echoes with the rhythmic sound of locomotive brakes, overhead automated announcements, and rolling wheelsets
Intersects major urban transit modes with direct access to subways, taxis, and commuter bus bays

facts_and_myths.claim: Grand Central Terminal in New York City has 44 passenger platforms and 67 tracks, more than any other train station in the world.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spread across two subterranean levels, Grand Central covers 48 acres in midtown Manhattan.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The terminal also houses a secret underground track, Track 61, once used by President Franklin D. Roosevelt.

facts_and_myths.claim: Standard passenger railway train tracks run completely loose on gravel ballast without any fasteners.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Steel rails are firmly clamped with elastic spring clips to heavy concrete or wooden railroad ties (sleepers), which are packed in angular stone ballast to absorb vibrational loads.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Continuous welded rail eliminates the historic 'clickity-clack' wheel joint sounds.

name: Subway Metro Station
visual_anchor: Underground metro station cavern lined with glazed ceramic tiles, an electric commuter train pulling into the platform with headlights illuminating steel tracks and third-rail insulators.
core_traits: Facilitates underground rapid rail transit across dense metropolitan urban centers
Equipped with subterranean platforms, automated turnstiles, descending escalator banks, and wayfinding maps
Accompanied by the whoosh of tunnel air displacement, squealing steel flanges, and electrified third rails
Features safety platform screen doors, route indicator boards, and emergency station master kiosks

facts_and_myths.claim: The London Underground, opened in 1863, was the world's first subterranean passenger railway system.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Its initial line between Paddington and Farringdon carried over 38,000 passengers on its opening day using steam locomotives.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The London network is affectionately known worldwide as 'the Tube' due to its deep circular bored tunnels.

facts_and_myths.claim: Subway trains are powered by ordinary diesel engines running inside subterranean tunnels.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Virtually all modern underground subways are 100% electrified, drawing high-voltage DC current from a trackside third rail or overhead catenary to prevent asphyxiating tunnel fumes.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Subway trains use regenerative braking to feed electricity back into the power grid as they decelerate.

name: Bus Terminal
visual_anchor: Bustling central bus interchange at dusk with numbered boarding slip lanes, sleek long-distance coaches reversing with warning beeps, passenger waiting concourses, and overhead departure screens.
core_traits: Acts as a centralized hub connecting local municipal bus lines and long-distance intercity motor coaches
Organized into designated sawtooth boarding bays, passenger waiting lounges, and ticketing kiosks
Characterized by the hiss of pneumatic air brakes, diesel engine idling, and baggage compartment loading
Provides travelers with multimodal connections to taxis, suburban rail, and city pedestrian centers

facts_and_myths.claim: The Port Authority Bus Terminal in Manhattan, New York, is the world's busiest bus terminal by passenger volume.
facts_and_myths.explanation: It serves approximately 225,000 passenger trips and several thousand bus movements every single business day.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The multi-level terminal features dedicated direct ramps into the Lincoln Tunnel to bypass surface traffic.

facts_and_myths.claim: City bus terminals only serve local neighborhood transit routes within a single metropolitan district.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Most major terminals integrate both local urban bus routes and extensive nationwide intercity motor coaches.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Intercity coach travel remains one of the most carbon-efficient mass transit options available.

name: Harbor Seaport
visual_anchor: Expansive coastal deep-water seaport at twilight with towering quayside gantry cranes, massive cargo vessels moored along granite wharves, tugboats kicking up white foam, and green navigation buoys blinking.
core_traits: Provides deep-water berths and handling facilities for ocean freight, cargo ships, and maritime commercial trade
Equipped with quays, mooring bollards, cargo container storage yards, and heavy-lift gantry cranes
Operates under the command of harbor pilots, harbor masters, customs enforcement, and stevedores
Shielded from open ocean swells and storms by engineered breakwaters, seawalls, and natural coastal bays

facts_and_myths.claim: Over 80% of all international trade in goods by volume is transported by maritime sea shipping through world ports.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Maritime shipping remains the most economically efficient method for transporting bulk raw commodities and manufactured consumer goods globally.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Port of Shanghai is the busiest container port in the world, handling over 47 million TEUs annually.

facts_and_myths.claim: Large container ships and bulk cargo vessels navigate freely into harbor slips without specialized pilot guidance.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Harbor law mandates that certified local maritime pilots board incoming vessels to navigate shallow channels, tides, and dockings with tugboat assists.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Pilots climb up rope Jacob's ladders on the hull of moving ships from small pilot cutters.

name: Lighthouse
visual_anchor: Tall red-and-white spiraled masonry lighthouse tower standing solitary on a jagged cliff edge amidst crashing ocean waves, its bright revolving lantern beam cutting through midnight sea fog.
core_traits: Emits powerful rotating beams of light to guide mariners, mark hazardous reefs, and signal harbor entrances
Features a towering cylindrical tower, an upper lantern room, and a service gallery deck
Historically utilized concentric Fresnel lenses to magnify and focus light rays over dozens of nautical miles
Produces distinct flashing patterns and low-frequency foghorn blasts for unique nighttime identification

facts_and_myths.claim: The ancient Lighthouse of Alexandria, built in Egypt in the 3rd century BC, was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Known as the Pharos of Alexandria, it stood over 100 meters tall and guided Mediterranean sailors with a massive fire and reflective mirror.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Greek word 'pharos' became the root for 'lighthouse' in many Romance languages, including French and Spanish.

facts_and_myths.claim: Every operational coastal lighthouse today is continuously manned by a live-in human lighthouse keeper.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Almost all modern lighthouses worldwide have been fully automated with electric halogen lamps, solar batteries, and remote telemetry.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The last manned lighthouse in the United States was automated in 1998 in Boston Harbor.

name: Gas Station
visual_anchor: Highway filling station brightly lit under an expansive illuminated canopy at night, glowing fuel pump displays, cars refueling at multiple pump islands, and an attached convenience mart with neon signs.
core_traits: Dispenses petroleum motor fuels such as gasoline and diesel from subterranean storage tanks to motor vehicles
Features multi-fuel dispensing pumps with flexible hoses, vapor recovery nozzles, and digital price meters
Operates under a sheltered structural canopy equipped with overhead fire-suppression chemical nozzles
Frequently integrates a 24-hour convenience market, windshield cleaning squeegees, and tire air compressors

facts_and_myths.claim: Fuel pump nozzles contain a tiny mechanical venturi tube that automatically shuts off fuel flow when the vehicle tank is full.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When liquid fuel rises and blocks the small air hole in the tip of the nozzle, a sudden pressure drop trips an internal diaphragm shut-off valve.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: This automatic safety mechanism is entirely mechanical and requires no electrical sensors.

facts_and_myths.claim: Using a mobile cell phone while pumping gas commonly causes catastrophic vapor explosions.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Extensive scientific testing by fire safety bodies and petroleum institutes found zero documented cases of mobile phones igniting fuel vapors.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Static electricity caused by drivers sliding across car seat upholstery is the primary culprit in rare fueling fires.

name: Multi-Story Parking Garage
visual_anchor: Tiered brutalist concrete parking structure at dusk with spiral vehicle entry ramps, rows of parked automobiles under fluorescent strip lighting, automated barrier gates, and ticket pay stations.
core_traits: Provides multi-tier vertical storage for automobiles to maximize vehicle capacity in dense urban centers
Equipped with inclined spiral vehicle ramps, painted parking stalls, pedestrian elevator shafts, and security cameras
Regulated by entry ticket dispensers, automated license plate recognition scanners, and barrier boom gates
Characterized by the sound of tires squealing on smooth coated concrete decks and low structural ceilings

facts_and_myths.claim: Automated mechanical parking garages use robotic pallet lifters to park cars without any human drivers inside the structure.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Robotic car parks store vehicles in compact honeycomb racks, stacking twice as many cars in the same footprint without ramps or pedestrian aisles.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The driver simply leaves the car in a ground-level transfer cabin.

facts_and_myths.claim: Modern parking garage floors are built completely flat without drainage slopes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Decks are engineered with deliberate 1% to 2% gradients and drainage channels to prevent water pooling, ice buildup, and road salt corrosive pooling.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Road deicing salts carried on car tires can severely corrode concrete rebar if water drainage is inadequate.

name: Suspension Bridge
visual_anchor: Colossal steel suspension bridge soaring across a wide oceanic strait at sunrise, twin majestic towers anchoring sweeping parabolic main cables, morning mist swirling around suspended highway decks.
core_traits: Spans vast water bodies or deep canyons by hanging the roadway deck from thick parabolic steel cables
Anchored by monumental vertical towers and massive shoreward concrete anchor blocks counteracting tension
Features vertical suspender wire ropes connecting the overhead main cable to structural stiffening trusses
Designed with aerodynamic deck profiles and expansion joints to safely flex under heavy winds and thermal shifts

facts_and_myths.claim: The main cables of colossal suspension bridges are spun on-site by pulling thousands of individual steel wires back and forth across the towers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: A single giant cable contains tens of thousands of galvanized high-tensile steel wires bundled and hydraulically compacted into a solid cylinder.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The Golden Gate Bridge cables contain enough individual wire to circle the Earth three times.

facts_and_myths.claim: A suspension bridge is engineered to remain completely rigid and must never sway or move in windstorms.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Suspension bridges are designed to flex, sway laterally, and rise or fall several feet with temperature changes to dissipate kinetic forces safely.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The 1940 Tacoma Narrows Bridge collapse led to modern aerodynamic wind-tunnel testing for all suspension bridge decks.

name: Ferry Terminal
visual_anchor: Busy waterfront ferry dock at sunset with a double-ended roll-on/roll-off vessel docking against wooden pilings, passenger boarding bridges deploying, and lines of waiting commuter cars on the approach apron.
core_traits: Facilitates maritime boarding and disembarkation for pedestrian commuters and motorized vehicles
Equipped with adjustable floating linkspan ramps that rise and fall with the coastal tides
Features vehicle staging lanes, passenger ticket lounges, overhead gangways, and mooring dolphins
Serves island communities, cross-bay urban transit routes, and coastal vehicular bypasses

facts_and_myths.claim: The Staten Island Ferry in New York City operates 24 hours a day and has provided completely free passenger transit since 1997.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Carrying over 20 million people annually across New York Harbor, it provides iconic views of the Statue of Liberty at zero fare.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: It has operated in some form since 1817, originally started by Cornelius Vanderbilt.

facts_and_myths.claim: Roll-on/roll-off (Ro-Ro) car ferries are impossible to tip over because cars are too light to affect ship stability.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Unsecured vehicular cargo or water entering open car decks creates dangerous 'free surface effect' shifts that can cause rapid catastrophic capsizing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Modern car ferries feature internal watertight subdivision bulkheads to compartmentalize any deck water.

name: Canal Lock
visual_anchor: Massive concrete canal chamber flanked by towering mitre gates, water churning violently as sluice valves equalize water levels, lifting a loaded cargo barge to the upper canal reach.
core_traits: Raises or lowers watercraft between stretches of water at different elevation levels on canals and navigable rivers
Composed of a rectangular chamber with watertight gates at each end and underground culverts with sluice valves
Operates entirely on simple gravity hydrostatic fluid pressure without requiring mechanical water pumps
Enables continuous commercial barge navigation across inland mountains, rapids, and waterfalls

facts_and_myths.claim: Leonardo da Vinci helped engineer the iconic chevron-shaped 'mitre lock gates' that seal tighter as water pressure builds behind them.
facts_and_myths.explanation: When closed at an upstream angle, hydrostatic water pressure forces the two wooden leaves firmly against one another, creating an automatic watertight seal.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Variations of da Vinci's 15th-century mitre gate design are still used on modern canals worldwide.

facts_and_myths.claim: The Panama Canal locks operate using giant electric water pumps to move millions of gallons into the chambers.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The Panama Canal works entirely by natural gravity flow; rainwater collected in elevated Gatun Lake flows downward to fill each lock chamber.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Each ship transit through the Panama Canal discharges roughly 52 million gallons of fresh water into the sea.

name: Helicopter Pad
visual_anchor: Elevated rooftop helicopter landing deck atop a modern glass skyscraper at dusk, painted with a bold white circled 'H' and touchdown circle, surrounded by green perimeter safety lights and a windsock fluttering against the city skyline.
core_traits: Designated reinforced landing and takeoff area specifically engineered for rotary-wing vertical aircraft
Marked with standardized visual navigation graphics including a prominent central 'H' and maximum weight limits
Equipped with omnidirectional perimeter floodlighting, elevated wind cones, and perimeter fall-safety nets
Installed on hospital rooftops for trauma evacuations, offshore oil platforms, and corporate skyscraper summits

facts_and_myths.claim: The bold circled 'H' marking on a helipad aligns so pilots can orient their aircraft approach into prevailing winds.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Standardized orientation and clear markings allow pilots to quickly judge approach paths, rotor clearance, and touchdown boundaries.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A red cross containing the 'H' signifies a dedicated hospital emergency medical helipad.

facts_and_myths.claim: Any flat skyscraper roof can safely serve as an emergency helicopter landing pad without structural modification.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Helipads require reinforced structural load-bearing trusses to withstand dynamic hard-landing impacts, plus specialized fuel drainage traps and foam fire suppression.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Turbulent rooftop vortex winds around tall buildings require strict flight approach certifications.

name: Highway Toll Booth
visual_anchor: Multi-lane highway toll plaza spanning a wide concrete expressway, electronic overhead overhead gantry transponder sensors blinking green, manual toll booths under a wide cantilever roof, and speeding headlights.
core_traits: Collects highway user fees, bridge tolls, or turnpike access charges from motor vehicles
Features multiple segregated traffic lanes, toll collection booths, crash attenuation barriers, and boom gates
Utilizes automated electronic toll collection (ETC) transponders, RFID tags, and high-speed overhead license cameras
Funds expressway capital construction, road repaving maintenance, and bridge structural inspections

facts_and_myths.claim: High-speed open-road tolling systems can accurately charge vehicles traveling at over 100 miles per hour without slowing down.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Overhead gantry antennas read RFID transponders and trigger synchronized high-speed infrared cameras to capture number plates in milliseconds.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Open-road tolling has eliminated traffic bottleneck backups at traditional physical toll booths.

facts_and_myths.claim: Toll roads were invented in the 20th century exclusively for modern motorized automobiles.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Turnpike toll roads have operated since antiquity; travelers paid tolls to cross private roads and bridges in ancient Greece, Rome, and medieval England.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The word 'turnpike' originated from a rotating pike-tipped timber barrier that was swung open after toll payment.

name: Air Traffic Control Tower
visual_anchor: Slender architectural tower rising high above an airfield, topped by an angled glass observation cab commanding 360-degree views of active runways, taxiways, and approaching jetliners in dusk skies.
core_traits: Directs aircraft ground movements, takeoff authorizations, runway crossings, and landing clearances
Features a 360-degree panoramic glass cab with outward-canted anti-reflective windows to reduce interior glare
Equipped with surface movement radar displays, flight progress strips, meteorological readouts, and radio transceivers
Manned by licensed air traffic controllers communicating with pilots via standard aviation phraseology

facts_and_myths.claim: The windows in the control cab at the top of an air traffic tower are tilted outward at a roughly 15-degree angle.
facts_and_myths.explanation: The downward tilt eliminates reflections of interior lighting and console screens on the glass, providing controllers an unobstructed view outside at night.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: The glass is also heavily tinted and heated internally to prevent condensation and frost formation.

facts_and_myths.claim: Air traffic controllers in the tower track and guide flights all the way across the entire ocean.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Tower controllers manage only immediate runway and airport taxiway movements within about 5 miles; en-route flights are managed by regional radar centers.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: High-altitude flights across oceans are managed by oceanic area control centers relying on satellite data.

name: Cable Car Station
visual_anchor: Alpine terminal station framed by massive spinning steel bullwheels and heavy tension cables, colorful enclosed passenger gondola cabins gliding smoothly out from the station over mist-covered pine valleys.
core_traits: Serves as the boarding terminal and mechanical drive station for aerial ropeways and cable gondolas
Houses massive motorized drive bullwheels, hydraulic cable tensioners, and track ropes
Features automated cabin decelerator tracks allowing passengers to board slowly moving cabins safely
Transports tourists, skiers, and commuters up steep mountain faces or across urban river gorges

facts_and_myths.claim: In modern detachable gondola lifts, cabins unclamp from the high-speed haul cable upon entering a station to crawl through slowly for passenger boarding.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Spring-loaded mechanical grip mechanisms release the main fast cable and transfer cabins to rubber tire conveyors, reclamping as they exit.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: This innovation allows cabins to cruise at 15 mph between stations while slowing to walking speed for boarding.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cable car cabins contain their own independent heavy internal combustion engines to propel themselves along the cables.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Cabins carry no motors; they are passively towed by a continuously moving loop of steel wire rope driven by a stationary electric motor in the base station.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Counterweight towers or hydraulic rams keep the cables taut under shifting passenger loads.

name: Cruise Ship Terminal
visual_anchor: Gleaming multi-level waterfront cruise terminal with soaring glass facades, colossal multi-deck ocean liner moored alongside, enclosed mobile passenger boarding gangways, and luggage transfer trucks on the apron.
core_traits: Processes thousands of passenger embarkations and disembarkations for ocean cruise voyages
Features vast baggage drop zones, customs and border immigration halls, security screening, and VIP lounges
Equipped with deep-water piers, heavy mooring bollards, shore-power electrical hookups, and fuel provisioning barges
Acts as a major tourism gateway connecting ocean travel with ground shuttles, hotels, and tourist attractions

facts_and_myths.claim: Modern cruise terminals can process luggage and security for over 6,000 passengers embarking on a single mega-ship in just a few hours.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Advanced RFID luggage tracking, staggered arrival check-in times, and facial-recognition biometric customs enable rapid processing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A mega cruise ship takes on hundreds of tons of food and fresh provisions during a standard single-day port turnaround.

facts_and_myths.claim: Cruise ship terminals are simple open docks without customs or passport control checkpoints.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Because cruise ships travel through international maritime waters, cruise terminals operate identical border security and immigration protocols to international airports.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Terminal officers check passports, visas, and contraband before passengers are allowed to step foot onshore.

name: Highway Rest Stop
visual_anchor: Sprawling highway service oasis off an interstate at night, illuminated high-rise fuel brand signboards, commercial truck parking lots with idling semi-trucks, 24-hour food court, and grassy pet walking areas.
core_traits: Provides travelers on long-distance limited-access expressways a safe location to rest, refuel, and dine
Contains public restrooms, dining courts, convenience shops, electric vehicle chargers, and fuel islands
Includes designated overnight parking areas for long-haul freight semi-trucks and commercial coaches
Features tourist information display racks, state highway maps, vending machines, and outdoor picnic tables

facts_and_myths.claim: Highway rest stops were strategically introduced on interstate highway systems to reduce driver fatigue crashes.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Mandated rest plazas give drivers a safe pull-off opportunity every 30 to 50 miles, drastically curtailing drowsy driving accidents.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Commercial truck drivers are legally mandated to log statutory rest breaks at designated rest stops.

facts_and_myths.claim: All highway rest stops are privately owned convenience stores that receive no public oversight.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Many rest areas are owned and operated by state or national departments of transportation to guarantee free public restrooms and water.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: State travel plazas often showcase regional agricultural foods and local artisan heritage displays.

name: Railway Freight Depot
visual_anchor: Vast labyrinth of parallel steel rail tracks stretching across a freight marshalling yard under towering floodlight towers at night, heavy diesel locomotives shunting long lines of boxcars and tank wagons.
core_traits: Sorts, groups, and marshals freight railcars into scheduled freight trains by final destination
Features humped sorting tracks, automated rail retarders, switching turnouts, and intermodal transfer cranes
Accompanied by the deep rumble of diesel freight engines, squealing brake shoes, and clanking steel couplers
Handles bulk commodities such as grain, coal, chemicals, manufactured automobiles, and lumber

facts_and_myths.claim: In 'hump yards', railcars are pushed over an artificial hill and coast freely downhill into designated classification tracks using gravity.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Pneumatic or hydraulic track retarders automatically grip the rolling wheels to slow cars to a safe coupling speed as they roll onto their assigned track.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A major modern hump yard can sort several thousand railcars in a single day.

facts_and_myths.claim: Rail freight uses far more diesel fuel per ton of cargo moved than long-haul highway semi-trucks.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Trains are roughly 3 to 4 times more fuel-efficient than trucks because steel wheels on steel rails experience dramatically lower rolling resistance.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: A single freight train can carry the equivalent cargo load of several hundred highway tractor-trailers.

name: Container Port Terminal
visual_anchor: Mega-scale coastal container terminal beneath rows of colossal ship-to-shore gantry cranes, towering stacks of multicolored 40-foot shipping containers, and automated guided vehicles moving along the wharf.
core_traits: Loads and unloads standardized intermodal shipping containers (TEUs) between ocean ships, trains, and trucks
Dominated by towering rail-mounted ship-to-shore (STS) gantry cranes with telescoping spreader beams
Organized into precision-surveyed container storage yard blocks managed by terminal operating algorithms
Operates around the clock with straddle carriers, reach stackers, and automated yard cranes

facts_and_myths.claim: The standardized 20-foot and 40-foot intermodal steel shipping container revolutionized modern global commerce in the 1950s.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Invented by Malcolm McLean, standardized containers eliminated manual break-bulk cargo loading, reducing shipping costs and turnaround times by over 90%.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Container ship turnarounds were cut from several weeks to less than 24 hours.

facts_and_myths.claim: Containers are stacked randomly on open dock concrete without computer planning or weight balancing.
facts_and_myths.explanation: Complex stowage planning software calculates vessel stability, weight distribution, and destination port offloading sequences to prevent ship capsizing.
facts_and_myths.fun_fact: Heaviest containers are always placed lowest in the ship's hold to keep the vessel's center of gravity low.

name: Dry Dock Shipyard
visual_anchor: Enormous drained concrete drydock basin holding an immense ocean vessel propped up on keel blocks, industrial shipyard cranes towering overhead, and welders' sparks showering down the massive steel hull.
core_traits: Enables the inspection, maintenance, hull repair, and construction of large ships in a drained waterless basin
Features a deep lock chamber with a removable floating caisson gate and high-capacity dewatering pumps
Vessels are floated into the flooded basin, the gate is sealed, and millions of gallons of water are pumped out
Allows shipwrights and marine engineers full access to the ship's keel, propellers, rudders, and bottom hull plates
